2609.25715.title: LingLan: An Advancing Traditional Chinese Medicine Diagnosis LLM with Multimodal Data
2609.25715.paper_summary: Though artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly transforms modern medicine, its integration into Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has been relatively slow, primarily due to TCM's reliance on holistic, subjective diagnostic methods---namely Inspection, Auscultation and Olfaction, Inquiry, and Palpation(I-AOI-P)---which are difficult to align with quantitative, standardized medical systems. In this work, we introduce a Unification Framework for Multimodal Data (UFMD), which automatically processes tongue and pulse images into structured, clinically standard descriptions, integrating multi-source diagnostic information into a unified digital record of I-AOI-P process. Building on this structured data, we create LingLan-14B, a TCM-specific large language model fine-tuned via supervised learning to emulate the diagnostic logic and workflow of I-AOI-P process. Experimental results show that our method significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, achieving a relative improvement of 103.5% over the baseline (62.72% vs. 30.82%) and reaching an F1-score of up to 82%.
2609.25715.paper_summary_zh: 儘管人工智慧（AI）日益改變現代醫學，但其在傳統中醫（TCM）中的整合相對緩慢，主要是因為中醫依賴於整體的、主觀的診斷方法——即觀察、聽診與嗅診、詢問和觸診（I-AOI-P）——這些方法難以與定量、標準化的醫療系統對齊。在這項工作中，我們介紹了一個多模態數據統一框架（UFMD），該框架自動將舌頭和脈搏圖像處理成結構化的臨床標準描述，將多來源的診斷信息整合到I-AOI-P過程的統一數字記錄中。在這些結構化數據的基礎上，我們創建了LingLan-14B，這是一個針對中醫的特定大型語言模型，通過監督學習進行微調，以模擬I-AOI-P過程的診斷邏輯和工作流程。實驗結果顯示，我們的方法顯著提高了診斷準確性，相較於基準提高了103.5%（62.72% vs. 30.82%），F1-score達到82%。
